content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe the major hormones and their functions
Explain how hormone levels are controlled
Understand the concept of target organs and receptors

are chemical messengers that coordinate many body functions. They are produced by endocrine glands and travel through the blood to affect target organs. This lesson provides an overview of the major hormones, their functions, and how they work together to maintain body homeostasis.
Stimulus triggers hormone release from gland
Binds to receptors on target cells
Stimulates growth of bones and muscles
More ADH = more water reabsorbed = concentrated urine
Less ADH = less water reabsorbed = dilute urine
Present in small amounts in females too
Most hormones take time to produce effects (except adrenaline)
Each hormone has only one function
Many hormones have multiple effects on different target organs
Testosterone is only in males, oestrogen only in females
Both sexes have both hormones, just in different amounts
Insulin is only important for diabetics
Insulin is essential for everyone's blood glucose regulation
Organ that responds to a specific hormone
Protein that binds specifically to hormone
Response opposes change to maintain stability
Ductless gland secreting hormones into blood
Hormones are chemical messengers traveling in blood
They affect target organs with specific receptors
Major glands: pituitary, thyroid, adrenal, pancreas, gonads
Pituitary controls many other glands (TSH, FSH, LH, ACTH)
Adrenaline causes rapid "fight or flight" response
Insulin and glucagon work antagonistically for blood glucose
Reproductive hormones control sexual development and reproduction
Most hormones controlled by negative feedback
